questions.question: What is the normal MRI appearance of a healthy tendon across all standard imaging sequences?
questions.detail: A normal, healthy tendon is characterized by low signal intensity (dark) on all standard MRI sequences.

questions.question: The magic angle artifact occurs when tendon fibers are oriented at which specific angle relative to the bore of the magnet (B0)?
questions.detail: Due to the anisotropy of tendon fibers, artifactually increased signal occurs when the tendon is oriented 55 degrees relative to the main magnetic field.

questions.question: Which of the following MRI parameters is most susceptible to the magic angle artifact?
questions.detail: The magic angle artifact is specifically seen on short TE sequences, such as T1-weighted or proton density (PD) images.

questions.question: How can a radiologist reliably distinguish magic angle artifact from true tendon pathology on MRI?
choices: The signal remains high on T2-weighted sequences.
The signal disappears on sequences with a long TE.
The tendon appears thickened and enlarged.
The signal is only seen on gradient-echo sequences.
questions.detail: Unlike true pathology, the magic angle artifact disappears with a long TE (e.g., T2-weighted images), and the tendon will maintain normal morphology.

questions.question: What is the characteristic MRI finding of tenosynovitis on fluid-sensitive sequences?
choices: Fluid completely surrounding the tendon circumferentially
A 'celery stalk' appearance of the tendon fibers
Fluid tracking only along the deep surface of the tendon
Signal that follows fat on all sequences
questions.detail: On MRI, tenosynovitis (inflammation of the tendon sheath) appears as fluid completely surrounding the tendon.

questions.question: Which term is preferred to describe age-related or overuse-related tendon changes, as the underlying process is typically not inflammatory?
questions.detail: Aging or overuse leads to myxoid degeneration (clinically synonymous with tendinosis); the term 'tendinitis' is discouraged because the process is not primarily due to inflammation.

questions.question: Which statement regarding the MRI appearance of tendinosis (myxoid degeneration) is correct?
choices: It is characterized by low signal on all sequences.
It always involves a complete gap in the tendon fibers.
It shows intermediate intra-substance signal on both T1 and T2 images.
It can be easily distinguished from a partial-thickness tear.
It is only seen in pediatric patients.
questions.detail: Tendinosis demonstrates intermediate intra-substance signal, and the tendon may be normal or enlarged. Importantly, MRI cannot reliably distinguish between myxoid degeneration and a partial tear.
